models_evaluated: Mortality prediction machine-learning model developed by Brajer et al. (2020)

links.outcome: Provider-perceived workflow disruption from mortality notifications and ACP documentation expectations
links.effect: Twelve of 22 providers (55%) responded; 83.3% reported no workflow disruption.
links.quote: When asked whether the ACP implementation was disruptive to workflow, 83.3% of respondents reported it was not.

links.outcome: ACP discussion documentation after provider education on the mortality-alert response workflow
links.effect: Documentation increased from three of eight patients (37.5%) before education to three of seven (42.9%) afterward; p =.999. All documented ACP discussions used bookends.
links.quote: As seen in Figure 1 , out of the eight patients in the pre-education group, three (37.5%) had an ACP conversation documented, compared to three out of seven (42.9%) in the post-education group, which was not significantly different ( p =.999).

links.outcome: Patients missed by model routing because of inaccurate admitting-service classification
links.effect: Some patients inaccurately admitted under “hematology” were not captured. In November 2022, model eligibility expanded to both services; the missed-patient count was not reported.
links.quote: In November 2022, the model was again adjusted to include patients with hematologic malignancies admitted under both the “hematology” and “hematology oncology” service, since data analysis indicated some patients were inaccurately admitted under the “hematology” service and had thus not been captured by the model.

unlisted_practices: Standardized Epic bookend documentation to make advance care planning discussions prompted by mortality alerts easily accessible.

links.effect: Of 12 responding providers, 83.3% reported the advance care planning alert implementation was not disruptive to workflow.
links.quote: When asked whether the ACP implementation was disruptive to workflow, 83.3% of respondents reported it was not.

links.effect: Data analysis revealed some patients were not captured by the model because they were inaccurately admitted under the "hematology" service rather than "hematology oncology".
links.quote: In November 2022, the model was again adjusted to include patients with hematologic malignancies admitted under both the “hematology” and “hematology oncology” service, since data analysis indicated some patients were inaccurately admitted under the “hematology” service and had thus not been captured by the model.

links.effect: A post-deployment survey found 75% of providers considered the model efficient and 83.3% felt the flagged patients were appropriate for the intervention.
links.quote: Additionally, 75% of providers felt the mortality prediction model was an efficient method for identifying at-risk patients, and 83.3% of providers felt that patients flagged by the model were appropriate for ACP.

links.effect: The model initially flagged fewer patients than expected for increased mortality risk, prompting a threshold adjustment to include medium-risk patients.
links.quote: Fewer patients than expected were flagged as being at increased risk of mortality. Therefore, in July 2022, the prediction model was adjusted to include patients at medium risk of mortality, in addition to high and critical risk.

unlisted_practices: Providing clinicians with specific electronic health record documentation tools (bookend templates) alongside predictive risk notifications to standardize and improve accessibility of advance care planning notes.
